executive_summary: Quality Holdings Resources has established credible board-level oversight of climate risk and discloses its operational emissions against a recognised standard, placing it ahead of many ASX-listed peers of comparable size. The disclosure weakens materially on forward-looking content: scenario analysis is referenced but not quantified, and no Scope 3 inventory is presented, leaving the largest component of the group's likely footprint unmeasured. Closing the Scope 3 and transition-planning gaps would move the company from partial to substantive alignment with AASB S2.

governance.narrative: The Board Risk and Sustainability Committee holds formal responsibility for climate-related risks and reviews them quarterly under a charter updated in FY2025. Management accountability sits with the Chief Operating Officer, who reports to the Committee at each scheduled meeting, and the Committee in turn reports to the full Board twice yearly. Two directors are identified as holding relevant environmental and resources experience. The disclosure does not establish whether climate performance forms part of executive remuneration, which remains the principal gap in an otherwise complete governance picture.

strategy.narrative: The company identifies physical risks to its Queensland operations from flooding and extreme heat, and transition risks arising from carbon pricing and changing customer requirements, assessed across short (to 2027), medium (to 2035) and long-term (to 2050) horizons. It states that scenario analysis has been undertaken but names only a generic 'high emissions' case, with no 1.5°C or well-below-2°C scenario disclosed and no quantified outcome presented. References to a transition plan describe intent rather than committed actions, assumptions or dependencies, and no financial effects are quantified.

risk_management.narrative: Climate risks are identified through the group's annual enterprise risk review and recorded in the same risk register as other material risks, which demonstrates genuine integration into existing processes rather than a parallel climate-only exercise. Risks are rated on the group's standard likelihood and consequence matrix. The disclosure does not state the materiality threshold at which a climate risk is escalated to the Board, nor describe the specific mitigation actions attached to the risks identified, leaving the management half of the pillar substantially thinner than the identification half.

metrics_targets.narrative: The company discloses Scope 1 emissions of 412,000 tCO2-e and market-based Scope 2 emissions of 58,000 tCO2-e for FY2025, prepared under the GHG Protocol using an operational control boundary, and states an intention to reduce operational emissions. No Scope 3 inventory is presented and no category screening is described, which for a resources group is likely to leave the majority of the footprint unreported. The reduction intention carries no base year, no target year and no stated scope coverage, so it does not constitute a disclosed target, and no external assurance is referenced.

findings.summary: Strategy disclosure is present but incomplete against the AASB S2 criteria.
Risk Management disclosure is present but incomplete against the AASB S2 criteria.
No Scope 3 emissions figures were found in any provided document.
Governance is the strongest pillar, supported by 4 pieces of evidence across the provided documents.

recommendations.text: Run and disclose a quantified scenario analysis that includes a well-below-2°C pathway alongside the existing high-emissions case, stating the assumptions used and the resulting effect on the Queensland asset portfolio.

State the materiality threshold at which an identified climate risk is escalated from the Group Risk Register to the Board Risk and Sustainability Committee, and record the mitigation action attached to each climate risk already on the register.

Publish a Scope 3 screening across the GHG Protocol's fifteen categories identifying which are relevant to the group, and disclose estimates for purchased goods and services and downstream transportation even if directional in the first year.
